### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.files

### Question

I have this in my lua file which used to work. Currently, 'g.' and 'g ' does not seem to work. Anyone has any idea how to fix this?

This is also related to https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/pull/1327#issuecomment-2462240594. The 'l' keybind still works as expected.

The reason I use 'g ' to toggle CWD is also for my grep search. I use `Snacks.picker` if it helps.

```
    -- Create mapping to show/hide dot-files
    local show_dotfiles = true
    local filter_show = function() return true end
    local filter_hide = function(fs_entry) return not vim.startswith(fs_entry.name, '.') end
    local toggle_dotfiles = function()
      show_dotfiles = not show_dotfiles
      local new_filter = show_dotfiles and filter_show or filter_hide
      MiniFiles.refresh({ content = { filter = new_filter } })
    end
    -- Create mapping to set current working directory
    local files_set_cwd = function()
      -- Works only if cursor is on the valid file system entry
      local cur_entry_path = MiniFiles.get_fs_entry().path
      local cur_directory = vim.fs.dirname(cur_entry_path)
      vim.fn.chdir(cur_directory)
    end
    -- Create mapping to go in if entry is a directory (I.E. do not open buffer if entry is a file)
    local go_in_if_dir = function()
      if (MiniFiles.get_fs_entry() or {}).fs_type ~= 'directory' then return end
      MiniFiles.go_in()
    end
    vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('User', {
      pattern = 'MiniFilesBufferCreate',
      callback = function(args)
        local buf_id = args.data.buf_id
        -- Tweak left-hand side of mapping to your liking
        vim.keymap.set('n', 'g.', toggle_dotfiles, { buffer = buf_id })
        vim.keymap.set('n', 'g ', files_set_cwd, { buffer = buf_id })
        vim.keymap.set('n', 'l', go_in_if_dir, { buffer = args.data.buf_id })
      end,
    })
```

comment_data.body:
Hello @mau-mauricelim,

Thanks for the question!

The code you provided is correct. Also, given the neovim config in your dotfiles, the 'g.' seems to work as expected. I checked the following:

1. `:lua MiniFiles.open()`
2. `:map g.`

The output: `n  g.          *@<Lua 1295: ~/.config/nvim/lua/plugins/custom/MiniFiles.lua:53>`

Can you apply these steps on your machine and provide the output of `:map g.`?

Regarding `g ` as `files_set_cwd`: In your dotfiles `g~` is used. Both `g ` and `g~` also work as expected. 

The snacks.picker is not relevant here, as the mappings are buffer-local and only apply when the explorer provided by `mini.files` has the focus.

I tested with the latest nightly and with version 0.12.6

> Hello @abeldekat, thanks for helping me look at this! I had a look again, and yes they indeed work BUT once the mini.files is closed. The pwd reverts back to the original one which the buffer was on (I think?).

Using your dotfiles, I cannot reproduce. After I close the explorer, the current working directory is still the one set when inside explorer.

That said, the neovim part of your dotfiles have been updated 6 months ago. The behavior you describe is consistent with [mini.misc](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/f9ac12d7cbd2563cfc2cce9a8152fc8df2ad0d6f/lua/mini/misc.lua#L431), `setup_auto_root`. Perhaps you started using that, or a similar plugin?
